# Claude Code transcripts made by hand

Transcripts for cases the live sessions in `../live/` do not cover, for `tests/claude_transcript.rs`. Made 2026-11-03
by a script (not kept) from the redacted live lines: every line is a live line with the same keys in the same order
and the same redaction (`../live/README.md`, "Redaction"); only the values named below were changed. The fake UUIDs
keep the numbers of the live case each line came from, so one file can mix them.

| File | Built from | What changed | The test expects |
|---|---|---|---|
| `broken-line.jsonl` | `03-loop-1m` lines 1 to 17 | line 10 (the first fire) cut short before its `cron` key, as a crash would leave it | the problem `transcript`/`line`, named only while the session holds anyway; the job still moved on by the fire at line 15 |
| `unknown-kind.jsonl` | `03-loop-1m` lines 1 to 9, 10, 19, 20 | the last three get kinds not seen yet: `subtype` `scheduled_task_fire_preview`, `type` `assistant_summary` and `user_echo` | no problem; the job keeps its `nextFireAt` |
| `missing-field.jsonl` | `05-reminder` lines 10, 11, 19 | no `id` in the `CronCreate` result, no `taskId` in the fire | no job; the first problem, `transcript`/`CronCreate result` |
| `seven-days.jsonl` | `03-loop-1m` lines 5, 6, then line 10 three times | the fires are at 2026-11-10 14:18:22.300, 14:19:22.300 and 14:20:22.300 UTC; the job was made 2026-11-03 14:19:24.194 | the first two move the job on, the third (7 days after its making) ends it; a process resumed at 14:19:30 that day drops it |
| `deleted.jsonl` | `03-loop-1m` lines 1 to 7, 19, 20 | a `CronDelete` of the job whose result is an error, one of an id no job has, then the real one | the job stays until the real delete |
| `carry-after-clear.jsonl` | `06-clear-during-loop.2` lines 1 to 9 | the carry line also has a one-shot in `tasks`, a daily job in `otherArmed`, a `wakeup` and an `ended` id, as Claude Code 2.1.317 can write it | read alone (Wakeshot started after the `/clear`): the four due times |
| `resume.jsonl` | `05-reminder` 10, 11; `08-sdk-bg-shell` 3 to 5; `09-resume-clean` 28, 29, 34, 35; `05-reminder` 10, 11 again; `13-sdk-resume-kill` 18; `09-resume-clean` 50 | one SDK session id, `entrypoint` `sdk-cli` and one `cwd` on every line; the second one-shot is `34 18 3 11 *` at 14:23:41 UTC; the stopped notice names the shell of line 5 and comes at 14:25:01.200; the fire at 14:29:46.100 | for a process started at 14:25:00.000 UTC: the missed one-shot, the wakeup and the shell are gone, the `*/5` job counts from the start |
| `task-stop.jsonl` | `08-sdk-bg-shell` 4, 5, then 4 and 5 again as a `TaskStop` call and its result (2026-11-04) | the call is `TaskStop` with input `{task_id}` and a new tool id; the result is 2.1.317's shape `{message, task_id, task_type: "local_bash", command}` from its code, at 14:22:50 | as an SDK session: the shell opens, and the stop's result closes it with no notification |
| `monitor-timeout.jsonl` | `02-monitor` 18, 19, 23, then 23 again (2026-11-04) | the last line is the timeout's event at 14:21:35.991, 120 s after the result, with the housekeeping body (`<event>` only) that 2.1.317's code writes; not seen live | as an SDK session: no open task, one timer at the result's time plus 120 s, which the timeout's event does not change |
| `header-notice.jsonl` | `08-sdk-bg-shell` 4, 5, 8 (2026-11-04) | line 8's text starts with 2.1.317's header: its first line as is, its other lines as `<str N>`, then a blank line; not seen live | the notification closes the shell |
| `joined-notices.jsonl` | `08-sdk-bg-shell` 4, 5, those two again for a second shell `b2wpi8oy3`, then 8 (2026-11-04) | line 8 is the header and two notifications joined by a blank line (`completed`, `killed`), with `joinedNoticeLengths`; not seen live | each notification closes its shell |
| `ui-stop.jsonl` | `08-sdk-bg-shell` 4, 5, 6 (2026-11-04) | line 6, the `queue-operation` `enqueue`, is a stop from the app at 14:22:50.000: `<status>killed</status>` and the summary length of 2.1.317's text for it (`tUr`); no user line follows, since that passive notice is delivered only at a later prompt. Shape from the code; not seen live | as an SDK session: the shell opens, and the queued `killed` notice closes it |
